dedupe_keys.name: code aster open source finite element solver edf

description: code_aster is an open-source finite element solver for mechanics, thermal analysis and dynamics developed by EDF. The site read on 2026-09-26 gives 37 years of development, 4,600 verification test cases, about 2,000 citations in publications and a million lines of code, and reports the 2026 annual users meeting for code_aster and Salome-Meca held at EDF Lab Paris-Saclay. Coverage is general structural and thermal mechanics, used by EDF for its plants and by others in industry and research. The source is on GitLab under the GNU GPL version 3, so it is free to use, and the site offers install and download pages, documentation, learning material and a forum; the site is created and hosted by Simvia for EDF. Caveats: the product description page loads its content by script and could not be read, so feature details beyond the home page were not checked, and users need finite element expertise. Simulation uses are structural integrity and seismic or thermal loading analyses of nuclear plant components, as hazard exposure studies, and a mechanics solver inside digital twin workflows. Related records: platform-salome-numerical-simulation provides the pre and post processing used with code_aster, and platform-code-saturne-cfd is EDF's fluid dynamics solver.
